newsitem.title: POLAND: Prague small gains lead East European markets.
newsitem.headline: Prague small gains lead East European markets.

text.p: The Prague and Budapest bourses rose slightly this week while Warsaw fell in profit-taking from recent record highs.
Foreign buying spurred Slovenian shares, Romanian shares stayed strong, Croatian stocks were mixed, and the Slovak bourse eased.
The CESI Central European Share Index was flat this week, ending at 1,626.62 points.
PRAGUE

Czech major issues drifted in directionless trade throughout the week, but rises on the broader market helped the PX50 to another small gain. The index rose 7.7 points, or 1.4 percent in the period, to close on Friday at 565.2.
The most heavily capitalised stock, SPT Telecom, which has oscillated around 3,400 crowns for several weeks, gained 25 crowns over the week to 3,395.
Dealers say they have been expecting a wave of foreign buying to boost blue chips but it has failed to materialise.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian shares rebounded on Friday, offsetting this week's losses. The BUX index closed at 5,468.83 points, up 30.28 from last Friday.

Investment funds still had a lot of money to spend, traders said, adding that this week's price falls triggered new buying opportunities on Friday. But they said purchases were not as powerful as they had been earlier this year.
"The market recovered as there was a huge amount of money awaiting for action," said Agnes Haszon of Equilor brokerage.
"There are some fluctations on the market, still, I believe the trend is upward even if certain stocks are very expensive."
WARSAW

Polish shares fell in profit-taking this week after reaching successive 33-month highs but analysts said the market should rise slightly on Monday, signalled by Friday's strong buying after price-fixing.

"Monday and Tuesday will test demand. Yesterday and today tested supply, which is falling, and now the question is if there'll be demand on Monday and Tuesday...If not, growth could end after one or two sessions," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Some analysts said primary market offers next month could prevent the recent stock-buying frenzy from returning.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed at 16,105.5 points on Friday, down 522.6 points or 3.1 percent from last Friday's close.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares jumped 6.3 percent this week, pushed up by extensive foreign buying. The ten-share SBI index soared 94.2 points to 1,573.6.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks ended the week on a firmer note with slight corrections among blue chips and further gains for hoteliers, and were expected to stabilise following recent steep gains.

This week's favourite -- food stock Podravka -- closed 12.89 percent higher at 359 kuna, but down from a record of 375 kuna. The group, renowned abroad for its food seasoning Vegeta, said on Thursday it would return to profit this year after selling loss-making subsidiaries and restructuring.
Traders said weak interest in leading issues -- drugs firm Pliva and particularly Zagrebacka Banka -- would likely cause their prices to ease before drawing back serious buyers.
Pliva closed at 500 kuna, down 13 from last week and Zagrebacka 20 kuna higher at 1,890, but was seen dipping to 1,800 kuna in the near term.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange continued its sluggish trading this week, with the 12-share SAX index sliding 1.21 points to 186.21 on Friday from Monday's opening.
Brokers said the market now seemed to be undervalued and they expected low prices to attract more foreign investors in the next few weeks.

"Prices have fallen to attractive levels, and we think that those investors now focusing on Poland, Hungary or Russia may turn their attention to Slovakia when those markets stop their current growth," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
BUCHAREST
The market's recent bull run lasted into this week pushing two unofficial indices to year highs but began to wane on Thursday, with investors focusing on few stocks.
Thursday's turnover of 802.9 million lei was this year's highest and all-time second highest.

Azomures fertiliser maker, which moved to the first tier this week, took the bulk of turnover from cross trades and a special deal struck outside the market on Thursday. It closed 3,300 lei stronger on the week at 24,000. JAN 30 CLOSE WEEK'S CHANGE 1996/97 HIGH 1996/97 LOW
